utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody, and sorry for that last-minute delay. It was beyond control. Mr. Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Laurie Sartorio for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. For the Defence, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, colleagues from the OTP. Good afternoon all in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas David Robson on behalf of the Defence of General Delic, assisted by assistant Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Good afternoon, Mr. Alija. May I remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony, to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Alija.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I hope that you have rested, that we shall be able to transact our business of your testifying quite quickly. We stopped at some reports of the 3rd Corps, and at this point I should like the witness to take a look at Exhibit 603. You will recall that yesterday the Prosecutor showed you this document also. This is a document of the Command of the 3rd Corps of the 8th of July, 1995, sent to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Kakanj command post, to the forward command post of the 3rd Corps and to the Command of the 7th Corps, and it is entitled "Regular Daily Combat Report." Please go to page 2 of the Bosnian version. The English version is on the screen, as it should be; the corresponding part, that is. Please, like you did yesterday, go through this part which describes the status and activities of the Corps forces in the zone of the 35th Division, and you will recall that yesterday you saw a reference to the -- to preparations being made for upcoming combat operations, together with the El Mudjahedin Detachment. Please remember this information as well as the date, which is the 8th of July, 1995. Keep it in mind. And for the time being, this document can then be moved away, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. We haven't seen the next page. I don't know what it is. You asked the witness to look at the status of the activities of the 35th Division. We haven't seen that yet, or is it -- the heading that I see is: "Current situation and activity of the 3rd Corps." That's the heading I have, not "35th Division."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Underneath that is "35th Division."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine, I see that, but that's not the heading she gave.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. The title is: "Situation and activities of the forces of the 3rd Corps," and the subtitle is: "The 35th Division," which is showed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you gone through this document? Have you seen this reference to the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honours, may the document be taken off the screen at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am. Yes, the document may be taken off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If, in connection with this document, document D577 can now be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this document states that it is a document of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Operative Planning Administration, it is a document of the 9th of July, 1995? The date which it bears is the 9th of July, 1995, and the title of it says: "Situation in the BH theatre of war on the 8th of July, 1995, report," or "information submitted to the president of the BH Presidency, to the army commander, to the GLOC Command in Visoko, the Moral Guidance Administration, Sarajevo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that this report also draws upon the daily combat reports from the Corps Commands for the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can page 2 of this document be shown to the witness now, please, and that is page 4, Your Honours, in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, until this page appears on the screen, please pay attention, like you did yesterday, to the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps, that is about midway down the page, and if the English version could also be scrolled down, please. There is a reference to the units of the 3rd Corps. Do you see that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you go through that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please follow -- do the same thing as you did before and tell us whether there's a reference to the El Mujahedin in it. This is fortunately the part which is legible, which refers to the activities of units of the 3rd Corps, but if you need assistance, I can give you a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not necessary. I can see it and I can read it also, and I can read it out aloud, if necessary, but there is no reference to the El Mudjahedin Detachment here at all. What it says is that the preparations for the execution of combat operations are being made, and engineer works as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can see the -- can we see the next page in the English version, please. And can we also see the next page in the Bosnian in order to demonstrate that no such reference is made elsewhere in this text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see that it goes on to speak about the 4th Corps. There is a section which refers to the security situation. Can you see the words "El Mujahedin" anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, page 7 of the English version, please, in order to show that -- for all of us to see that there is no reference to it on this page. Yes, the next page in English, please. That's it. That's it. And also can the witness be shown the last page of this document, which is page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that there is a handwritten indication here to the effect that the document was sent to the General Staff, cryptographically protected?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who is the signatory?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you assist us in this connection?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signatory is Brigadier Ferid Tabakovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is on the next page in the English version. Please explain to us who Mr. Tabakovic is.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the Operations Centre at the time, in the Operations Department, i.e., in the Administration for Operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned a duty officer who was on duty there to analyse these operations. Was Mr. Tabakovic his superior?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in charge of the team on duty in that particular instance, but otherwise he was the chief of the Operations Centre. The duty officer would collect all the data and draw up the memorandum with such information and Tabakovic would sign it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 617.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document can now be taken away. I should like the witness to take a look at Exhibit number 606.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I should just like to state for the record that this is a document of the Command of the 3rd Corps, dated the 18th of July, 1995, sent to the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Kakanj command post. The title of the document is: "Carrying Out Active Combat Operations." Do you remember the Prosecutor showing you this document, this report yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You remember that to the Prosecutor's questions, that you replied to questions by the Prosecution and Their Honours in this connection. Your Honours, we seem to be having a problem with the screen, with the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We notice that. It will be attended to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is being attended to. Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we can continue. Do you remember that yesterday the Prosecutor showed you item 1, which says that combat readiness for the upcoming task will be determined by the El Mudjahedin Detachment; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would not dwell upon this document. This document can be taken away. I would kindly ask the witness to remember the date, the 18th of July. This document can be moved away, and at this moment I would like to show the witness Exhibit number 537.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that you can see the document well on your screen. This is a document issued by the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Administration for Operational Planning. The date is 19 July 1995, and the document's title is: "The situation in the BH theatre of war on 18 July 1995." The information was sent to the president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army commander, the Command of the Main Logistics Centre in Visoko, the Administration for Morale Guidance in Sarajevo. And can you please look at the introductory sentence, and will you tell me whether you agree that a reference is being made to the combat reports from the Corps Command and the monitoring of the situation in the BH theatre of war in the course of 18th of July, 1995, and that this document also describes the characteristics of combat activities on that day? And I would kindly ask you to look at page 2 of this document.. Can you please show the witness page 2 of this document, both in B/C/S as well as in the English version. Your Honours, Witness, I'm going to ask you to do the same. Pay attention to the activities of the 3rd Corps. Can the English version be lowered down a little, because that part is towards the bottom of the English page. And here, Witness, in the upper half you have a reference to the 3rd Corps, first the 1st Corps, the 2nd Corps and finally the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that this is a very brief piece of information about combat activities that the 3rd Corps was involved in?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And will you agree with me that there's no information that we saw in the document that originated from the 3rd Corps and was sent to the command post in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The El Mudjahedin Detachment is not mentioned here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we also see the last page of the same document. Actually, can we see page 3 of this document, which is page 4 in the English version, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. The document was signed by the head of the duty team, Brigadier Tabakovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, somebody signed on Brigadier Tabakovic's behalf, but his name is here. I suppose that a duty operations officer signed on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And again we have an indication of cryptographic protection?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, this document has already been admitted into evidence, and now if we can move this document away, please, and I would like the witness to be briefly shown another document, Exhibit number 496.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put just one brief question to you. Given the fact that you drafted this document, you were its author, can you please confirm that this is a document issued by the General Staff of the Army on the 16th of July, 1995, and that this document was addressed to the Commands of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 7th Corps? Please look at item 3, and I'm going to ask you for your comment. Here, in the last line of bullet point 3, a reference is made to the places -- Your Honours should be shown the following page in the English version. Their Honours should be shown the following page in the English version, please. Thank you very much. I'm talking about the places which are referred to in the last line of bullet point 3 of this document. A reference is made to Cerska, Kamenica, Konjevic Polje and others. Please, Witness, since you are the author of this document, you can confirm, can't you, that Kamenica is a very common name of places in Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This refers to the place Kamenica which is near Srebrenica, but there are a dozen other places bearing the same name in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this is Kamenica in Podrinje, which has nothing whatsoever to do with Kamenica in the Vozuca area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it has nothing to do with it. This is an order that refers to Zepa and Srebrenica, and this Kamenica is near Srebrenica and Zepa and no other Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. Your Honours, could this document now be moved away?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document may be moved away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit number 605.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will remember, Witness, won't you, that yesterday the witness [as interpreted] showed you this document by the 3rd Corps, dated 3rd August 1995. This document is a regular combat report sent to the General Staff of the BiH Army at the Kakanj command post, the former command post of the 3rd Corps, Orahovo, the Command of the 3rd Corps in Postinje and the Commands of the 2nd and 7th Corps as well. Now I would kindly ask you to look at the second page of the same document, which is also true for the English version. Witness, in order to avoid wasting any more time, you can see the title "35th Division"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please pay attention to the part that concerns the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please retain this piece of information, and also can you please retain the date. The date of this document is the 3rd of August. I would like this document to be moved away, and now I would like the witness to be shown document D579. D579, please. For the record, Witness, just to make things clear, can you see that this is a document issued by the General Staff of the Army, Kakanj, dated 4 August 1995, and that this document again speaks about the situation in the theatre of war as on the 3rd of August, 1995; can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that the document was sent to the president of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to the Army commander, the GLOC commander in Visoko, the Administration for Moral guidance in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And also can you also see that in the introduction a reference is made to the situation in the theatre of war, based on the Corps Command reports as at the 3rd of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would kindly ask the witness to be shown page 2 of this document, and the same page in the English version. And I am going to ask the witness to look how the activities of the 3rd Corps are described in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is in the second paragraph from the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you to tell us whether there is any information about the El Mudjahedin Detachment or its activities.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems that in the English version, the title, "The 3rd Corps," has been omitted. I would like to draw your attention to that, or maybe if you scroll down the document a little, maybe we will see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, Witness, can you please read -- because of the situation, can you please read what it says about the 3rd Corps in the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will gladly do that: "The 3rd Corps --"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, slowly.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the area of the 303rd Mountain Brigade, at 1600 hours, attack combat activities were launched by our forces in the sector of Jasenovi, Ravne and Kosovnjak. The battle is ongoing. We have not received a report about the combat results. The other units are engaged in decisive defence." And this is what is written about the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. Your Honours, we will ask for a revision of this translation so as to make the exhibit clear. Now we have it on record as interpreted by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want it admitted, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And as you have a revised interpretation of that document, could you please, just for the sake of some of us, give the full meaning of the word "GLOC" which is on the heading on the first page? One of the addressees is "GLOC" something, G-L-O-C. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 618.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you explain to the Trial Chamber the meaning of the abbreviation "GLOC"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: GLOC: "G" is main, "L" is logistic and "C" is centre. This is the Main Logistical Centre which was located in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document may be moved away. At this moment, I should like to show the witness Exhibit number 370.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, unfortunately this document has been photocopied. I hope you see that. It says: "The General Staff of the BiH Army," that the document was drafted in Kakanj on the 29th of March, 1995. The title is: "The organisation of life and work at the command post of the Main Staff of the BH Army," and this is also an order to all administrations and departments and to the chief of the Operations Centre. Would you please look at the first page of the document and particularly to pay attention to the redeployment area, and to confirm for the Trial Chamber, since you worked there, whether it is correct that the following features and facilities were used in Kakanj as the facilities for the redeployment the Staff of the Supreme Command at the command post in Kakanj. First the Sretno Motel?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A part of the Kakanj Distribution Centre?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Part of the buildings and premises of the company for the overhaul of vehicles and its parking lot?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Part of the petrol building?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The stadium building?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The DP cement factory in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the Zening DT, Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was used in Zenica. I never paid a visit to that particular building. I don't know what was there. I believe that the Administration for Education and Training was there, and that there was also the Command of the Air Force. I suppose that these two were in that facility, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see the English version doesn't mention Zenica, it says "The Zening DT expansion unknown in Kakanj." But I can see in B/C/S that I see "DT Zening Zenica." Obviously, that needs correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We shall ask for a correction of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now just take a look at this part which concerns control and command, item 2, where it is stated: "When the commander is absent from the KM, the chief of Staff shall exercise command and control, and at a time when both of them are absent, command and control shall be assumed by the high-ranking officer or the one holding the highest position or an officer assigned by a special order of the commander or the chief of Staff."

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that it is written here. What I want to ask you is the following: Is it true that this is the way it actually functioned in practice in 1995, during the period when you were working there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was exactly the way it functioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now take a look at page 4 of this document. That, Your Honours, is also page 4 in the English version. And, Witness, I should like to ask you this: First of all, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Obviously, this was signed by Commander Rasim Delic. Do you agree that this document, which was produced in Kakanj, bears no indication whatsoever to the effect that the document is being sent anywhere under cryptographic protection?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is because at that particular time, General Delic was sitting there and he signed the document there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just check whether I understood you properly, Mr. Alija. When General Delic is sitting and working in Kakanj, no one else signs documents on his behalf, but he does with his own hand when he's in Kakanj; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If he is not in Kakanj, then someone will sign on his behalf, sign documents on his behalf, as regulated by this document; that is to say, it will be signed by General Hadzihasanovic or a person standing in for him, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I was just about to go back to the first page myself, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, I understand what you just asked the witness, that when General Delic is in Kakanj, he signs documents himself. Now, even though that may be the case, do the people who are the addressees not sign the document to confirm that they have received them, even if they are there in Kakanj? I would expect, given the practice so far, that they would actually at least sign to say, "Yes, we have received this document," even if it came by hand from the next-door office. Wouldn't that be the practice, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was not the practice, because the addressees of the document are quite clearly shown here, the administrations, the heads of departments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, all documents, the addressees are clearly shown, but usually they sign at the bottom that they have received the document. If what is ordered here has not been carried out, how does General Delic maintain discipline by saying -- to say that, "Look, I wrote this order, you received it. Here's proof that you received it. You didn't carry it out. Now I'm going to discipline you"; how would he do that if it is not signed by the addressee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After signature, this order would go to the Protocol Department, and the protocol Department, i.e., office, would then pass it on to all the indicated addressees. In the Protocol office, if we were to check against this date, we probably could find a reference to the order having gone to these respective administrations, so it would be known that it had gone to them, and someone there who received the document probably, in the administration concerned, signed such receipt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And where does the person sign the receipt if the receipt is not on the document, and if the General has to take disciplinary measures, must he now go to the Protocol Department to find out whether, indeed, the addressee did receive the document? I find this a little anomalous. To me, it would appear that even where it is not sent by cryptographic protection or it is not sent by post or courier, at least the recipient must indicate that he has received the document, even if he's in the same office. That's my view. But you say this was not done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can ascertain that by consulting the protocol book against this particular date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a bit more -- just another clarification in connection with this document. Do you agree with me that this document is addressed to administrations and departments which are in Kakanj and not in Sarajevo or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to the chief of the Operations Centre, who was also sitting in Kakanj; right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honours, if you have no questions in regard of this document, can I have it taken away?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can take it away, but your last question still doesn't answer my question. I'm accepting that these people sit in Kakanj, but I'm just saying it's surprising that they don't indicate acknowledgment of receipt, like it's done on all other documents. And I accept that they are in Kakanj, they're not in Sarajevo. The document may be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, once again, please, in situations when a document was submitted to the same place within -- in other words, within the Staff of the Supreme Command, to bodies within the Command, it is true that by consulting the protocol, we could see in the protocol book that the addressees, the persons -- recipients actually acknowledge receipt of such a document by their signatures?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reiterate, this was the procedure, this was the method of work: Once the commander or the chief of Staff signed a document or an order, it would go to the Protocol, and the protocol people would then distribute it among the administrations, and someone from the administration, whether it was a duty officer or the chief of the administration, would sign having received -- acknowledge receipt of such a document, and I'm quite sure that if we checked in the protocol office register, we would find the respective administrations of person's signature against the date in question in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing let's explain, Witness. The procedure is not the same with the documents if the person who receives the documents sits as a member of the body that the document is addressed to or if the person is outside the Supreme Command? Did you understand my question, can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in a situation when this person is a recipient outside the body of the Command, then there is no indication of that in the protocol, but it is seen on the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. There is an indication on the document, the date of dispatch and the initials of whoever dispatched it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If it is sent by courier, then the courier has to have a dispatch log where the courier will indicate having received documents and to whom he has submitted them; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, there is always a trace.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Is there still any quandaries about this, Your Honours? I shall do my best to prove the authenticity of this document, if that is in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam, we were long satisfied -- I was long satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can the witness now be shown document D580.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Witness, that what you see before you is a regulation on the internal structure and competence of the General Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that the date on it is the 24th of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a large document, Your Honours, and we have managed -- we have provided an excerpt from this document, and a translation of it. So please go to page 2 of the Bosnian version. I believe it is also page 2 in the English version. Please focus on this part, which says: "The commander of the chief -- of the General Staff of the Army." Working in this staff, the Supreme Command Staff, you certainly had occasion to see this document, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document. I saw this document when I was in the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You knew how the General Staff of the Army functioned. Do you agree that the competences of the Army General Staff were determined by the Law on Defence as well as by other regulations of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now focus on this second part of the document, where reference is made to the fact that the commander of the General Staff of the Army, in his absence, shall be represented by the chief of the Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with respect to units, corps and independent units, unless the commander of the General Staff of the Army has regulated this. Otherwise -- and by the deputy commander of the General Staff with respect to the organisational units of the General Staff. My question to you is the following: In the course of 1995, whilst you were working at the General Staff or at the Supreme Command Staff at the Kakanj command post, was this the way the representing, the deputizing for the commander functioned, that is, by the chief of Staff who was at the same time his deputy, General Hadzihasanovic, in other words?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go to page 3, the next page in the document now. Do you agree that this regulates -- or rather would you first go through it, read it, and then I'll ask you my question. The deputy commanders and the chiefs of the Organisational Staff, with respect to military units and installations, could have been given special authorities by the commander of the General Staff of the Army, who could have transferred to him his competences and responsibilities. Do you agree that this is the way it functioned in practice?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 619.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D581 at this point shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a recording of the 200-- a tape-recording of the 256th session of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on the 5th of August, 1994. Naturally, I'm not going to ask you about the substance of this meeting at which you were not present. I just want you to confirm a fact which is of bearing on our discussion up to this point. Please take a look first at this customary reference to the fact that the session is presided over by the President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to page 3 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is of bearing for me here is for you to confirm, Witness, that deputies stood in for General Delic also at Presidency sessions, and you were aware of that, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And we see the penultimate name here, "Divjak"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not hear the witness's answer because of the overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Vidovic. The interpreters did not hear the witness's answer because of the overlap, the overlap in between the two of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should repeat my question, Witness, to you, and it was this: It is true, is it not, that deputies of commanders, deputy commanders, in the absence of commanders, also attended Presidency sessions, such as this one as was the case in this particular instance where we have General Divjak sitting in that position?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. At that time, General Jovan Divjak was the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We ask for a translation of this document, Your Honours, and the minute we get it, I shall also insert it into the file and incorporate it into the document. But at this point, we would kindly ask for this document to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 620.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge Harhoff suggests it's get to be "MFI." Why, because we don't know the English version?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Marked for identification MFI --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right, fine, it will be 620 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pending the provision of the translation, did I get it right? Thank you very much, Your Honours. Thank you very much. Can this document now be taken off the screen, and I should like the witness to be shown the first of a batch of -- of the next batch of documents that we have prepared. Can the witness be shown document D416, please. Your Honours, let me just explain. This batch of documents, D416, consists of a number of documents. I'm going to ask the witness to just take a look at who issued the documents and who signed the documents, because we are not concerned with the substance of the documents. That is not of bearing to our task. And after he has seen all these documents, I'm going to ask him a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date is the 5th of September, 1955 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but what is the relevance, madam, if you are not going to see the body of the document? Surely, you are not expecting us, when we write the judgement, to look at the document and see the heading and see the signature, and it's empty, and what is it going to be telling us?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by this batch of documents that you are going to see, I wish to demonstrate something which is extremely relevant to the Defence, which is that in this period General Delic was represented. It is just a fact of General Delic's representation from the 5th to the 16th of September, 1995. This is what I want to show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I would suggest you ask those questions that establish that before you tender the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will certainly do so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us revert to the following: Can you take a look at this document, and do you agree that this is a document of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, issued on the 5th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We didn't understand each other. I'm suggesting that you ask questions to the witness which establish the point you were saying, and then when you have done so, get the witness, as you tender these documents, to confirm what you have said, rather than take in every document and ask him the same sort of questions with the same document -- you know, with each document as it comes. Ask the questions, and then you can tender your documents collectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. I didn't quite get it before. Thank you very much. I didn't understand you properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that in his absence, General Rasim Delic, in his absence from the command post, that is, he was represented by General Hadzihasanovic, who was the chief of Staff and, at the same time, his deputy, or by a person designated by the latter?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this period, that is to say, in September 1995, you were working at the Kakanj command post, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was the time of the September combat activities at Vozuca, if you recall, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly. I remember that there were activities. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember that General Hadzihasanovic represented General Rasim Delic in September 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at these documents to see who issued them, who is the issuer of the document, and who is the signatory, whether it is stated, in other words, for the commander, on behalf of the commander, and who is the signatory. Here we have a document of the 5th of September, 1995, issued by the General Staff of the Army, the Army Staff. Do you agree that it states: "Representing the commander" on the date in question, of course, Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic, and then it is signed? Can you tell us who it is signed by?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please slow down so that we can have the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I am speaking quite slowly. Yes, you are quite right. It is said here: "Representing the commander, Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic," and signing for him was Brigadier Asim Dzambasovic, who at the time was the chief of the Operations Planning Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we take a look at the next page. I will be tendering, Your Honours, all this as one exhibit. Here we have the -- it is a document of the General Staff of Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at Kakanj, from the 9th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that on this day, it was also Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic who was representing the commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And will you tell us who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is also Brigadier Asim Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Could we now go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is also a document of the General Staff of the Army, the Army Staff at Kakanj, dated the 10th of September, 1995, and I shall ask you the very same question. Is it true that on this day also, which is to say on the 10th of September, 1995, the commander was represented by Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And signed by --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also signed by Brigadier Enver -- Asim Dzambasovic. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can we take a look at the next page. We're waiting for the English version of the document dated 11 September. This is okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that on this day, the General Staff of the Army, the Staff of the Army in Kakanj, the date is 11 September? And I would like us to see the next page of the document. Just the signature block, please. In the English version as well. Next page in the English version, please. Will you agree with me that on this day, the 11th of September, 1995, the Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic was standing in for the commander; is that correct? Do you agree that this is his signature?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and, yes, this is the general's signature, General Hadzihasanovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the following page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I don't want to interfere with you. My suggestion was intended to cut down on the time you're taking on tendering these documents. I realise you've already gone beyond the time taken by the Prosecution by far, and I don't know how much more you still have to cross-examine this witness. You know, I'd hoped that when you'd established why you wanted to tender them, you'd just say -- at least get him to look at them quickly and then tender them, rather than ask him the same questions with respect to each document as it comes through, because you have laid the foundation for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And may I also intervene with a question. Is the purpose of this exercise to show that General Delic was absent in those days or is it to show that General Hadzihasanovic was replacing him during his absence, or both?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, both, and particularly the latter. He was represented by General Hadzihasanovic. Your Honours, I need another five to ten minutes. I'm almost at the very end of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that this is the last document in your list. But could I just ask the Prosecution if the fact that General Delic was absent in these days and was represented by General Hadzihasanovic, is that disputed by the Prosecution? Because if it is not, then I don't think we need to spend any more time on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The fact that he wasn't physically there is not disputed, Your Honour, but the fact that he was -- that is disputed, we argue that he was still in command and control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. Well, thank you very much. Please continue, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the reason, Your Honours. I believe you will appreciate this. I believe that the time has come for our break, and I can assure you that I will need only five more minutes, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, but I would like you to wrap up this exhibit before we go for the break. Could you please just wrap up this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just confirm for us, Witness, please, that this is a document issued by the Staff at the command post in Kakanj, the date is 13 September 1995, and that it says here: "Standing in for the commander, General Hadzihasanovic"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have just one more page to show to the witness. Can we please see the very beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me, Witness, that this is another document by the General Staff of the Army, the Army Staff in Kakanj, the date is 15 September, and will you agree with me that this document is an interim report which had to be sent to the Intelligence Administration, and that it was for the attention of the president of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at the signature block on the following page. The following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that it is indicated here again that the Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic is standing in for the commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this moment I would like to bring my cross-examination to an end. I would kindly ask for this set of documents to be given one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The documents are admitted into evidence, and may they please be given a single exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the collection of documents will be Exhibit number 621.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic. Is that the end of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take the break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. May the witness please be shown Exhibit 496 again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I think you've seen this document a few times in the last couple of days, and I would particularly like to draw your attention to the number of the document, which is 1/825-1276. Do you see that number at the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'd just like to draw your attention to what is stated in Item Number 4. And for the Judges, that will be on the next page, please. And in this item, sir, it appears, does it, that General Delic is asking for reports to be sent on a certain date, a certain time, and then also isn't he asking for subsequent reports to be sent on this matter? Sir, are you --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Just remember this number of the document, sir. And I would ask the document be put away, and I ask that document 494 be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit number 494, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, again at the top of the document do you see the number -- the same number, 1/825 -- oh, no, it's not the same number, excuse me, 1/825/1306. That's the number of this particular order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'd like to draw the witness's attention to number 3, and for the Judges it will be on -- if you scroll down -- number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, this also -- this document is from General Delic, correct, and in number 3 what is -- he's instructing the corps commanders that they are personally responsible to him to carry out these assignments; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, under item 3: "The corps commanders will be responsible for the execution of these tasks." Could you please scroll down a little, because I can't see the signature, and you specifically asked me who signed the document. And this is on behalf of General Delic, signed by another officer, and I suppose it was General Rasid Zorlak.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But it's on behalf of General Delic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on behalf of General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, if you go back to number 3, I just want to be more precise. In the English version, sir, it says that the General is ordering that the corps commanders be personally responsible to him; in other words, the word "me" is in the English version. Is that word in the Bosnian version, "they are responsible to me," is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in number 4, what is number 4? Number 4 is instructing that a report be sent to him by 2000 hours on the 18th of July; is that what number 4 says, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May this document be put away, and I would like the witness to now be shown Exhibit number 606.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree with me the date of this document is the 18th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if you look in the first sentence of the document, "in accordance with ..." And it lists two orders there. Are the two numbers the same two numbers -- are they the two numbers of the previous two orders that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And then when you look in number 1, and we've talked about this before, when -- it says that: "The El Mujahedin is the primary leader of the upcoming task"; is that what it says in number 1?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is indicated here, amongst other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So is this the report that General Delic ordered in the previous order that it be sent to him?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. The Prosecution suggests something that doesn't arise from any of the documents or from anything that the witness has testified to in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Testified to in his testimony or testified to during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor is putting a very leading question and suggests to the witness a construction that has nothing whatsoever to do with the document that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you are changing your ground now. I don't understand what -- I don't know what I must do now. Your first objection was because, you're saying, she's taking something that doesn't arise from any of the documents or from anything that the witness has testified to in his testimony, and I asked you, in his testimony or in cross-examination. Now you're coming up with leading questions which is not what was contained in your first thing. I've got to rule on one thing only. I can't rule on two objections at the same time, and I'm going to stick to the first one first. You can raise the second one later if you want to, but -- just a second. I want you to confirm to me that are you saying that what has been raised by the Prosecutor is something that the witness didn't testify to in his testimony or is it something that you didn't ask him about during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, what? I've put to you two questions, two alternatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this refers to both. The witness has never said anything to that effect either on chief or on cross. The Prosecutor suggested this is the document, and the witness has already spoken about this document, so my answer to your question would be: Neither. The witness has not said anything like that either on chief or on cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I'm sorry, you have not responded to my questions. I'm sorry, I'm going to have to overrule you, because I see that this document was referred to in cross-examination this morning, 606, and unless you can make a choice between my questions, I'm sorry, I've got to rule you out of order. I would accept you if you said -- not even accept, but I would put it to the Prosecution to respond if you said it was not raised in cross-examination. But if you are not making a choice between the questions I'm putting to you, then I'm going to rule you out of order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to choose, Your Honour. This document was raised on chief, and then in my cross I went back to this document. In other words, this does not arise from my cross-examination. This was part of the examination-in-chief. That is the essence of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any response, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, both of these documents were put in through this witness on direct, and then these documents were covered on cross, and I think the implications from the cross-examination were putting documents together, and that's what I'm trying to do at this point. I'm trying to draw the witness's attention to redirect on an area that the Defence spent an enormous amount of time on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, since we've -- yes. Can you answer the last question, sir, which -- can you tell, sir -- I guess I'll -- can you tell, sir, from the face -- from these two documents, given the reference numbers of the orders, whether these two documents are related?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Two documents or three documents? The two orders and the response?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, the three documents, whether there is a link -- a direct link between these three documents.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? Which two documents, the documents referred to herein or --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If I may go back to 494, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't worry. Let's just say this: Sir, you were shown Exhibit 496 with reference number 1/825-1276, and then you were shown Exhibit 494 with reference number 1/825-1306. Can you see those reference numbers in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see 1/852-25 and 1/825-1036.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 1306. It's 1276 and 1306. Can you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You remember seeing those two documents a couple of minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question to you now by the Prosecution is: Is there any relationship between those two documents and this document that is on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should have to look at these two documents again, by your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May the witness be shown 494 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you see the number 1/825-1306 at the top of this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what kind of number is this? Is this a reference number for the order?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the number under which this order was registered.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, go down to number 4, please. And for the Judges, it's on the second page. This is important. Does number 4 request that a report be submitted by the 18th of July, by 2000 hours; is that what that says?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness now be shown 606 again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you see the number at the top -- oh, no, excuse me, strike that. What time was this document dated -- what time was it stamped or sent? What is that time at the top left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states here: "2359".

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, what is the number that is down below underneath the day; what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "2000 hours." That means that that was the time at which the document -- the report was being written.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And the date of the document is the 18th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in the first sentence of that document, do you see the reference number 1/825-1306, which is the document that you just looked at a few minutes ago; correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In your experience, in your position as the chief of the Operations Centre at the Kakanj command post, at the Administration for Operative and Planning, can you tell us whether this document is a direct response to that order?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must correct you. I was not the chief of the Administration for Operations and Planning, but I was the chief of the department comprised within the Administration for Operative Planning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction, sir. Now can you answer the question, whether this document represents a direct response to that order?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report which is connected to the two previously-shown orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. This document may be put away. Now I'd like to show the witness a document which is PT6079. It's a -- actually, it's a videotaped interview of General Delic, and we have a section of that videotape we'd like to show to this witness and ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection. We have not received any indication that anything of the kind would be used, and we have not prepared our defence in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, this exhibit is on the Prosecution 65 ter exhibit list, and it was played in the opening of this case, and therefore the Defence is on plenty of notice that this document is going to be used, they've had plenty of time to review it, and this document is relevant, directly relevant to what was raised for the first time on direct examination which is the -- cross-examination, excuse me, which goes to General Delic being out of the country and who is in charge and who is in command. It goes directly to that issue, and it was raised in cross-examination and the Defence has notice that this document is going to be put in evidence. And it's very relevant and very important, especially in response to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm aware of you. I just want to get clarification on a point. Is it not one of the agreed facts that General Delic was out of the country at some stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe it is, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it is, why do you say it has been raised for the first time in cross-examination? Surely it's an issue that the parties were aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. It's not just him being physically out of the country, it's the representation -- the cross-examination implied that he was represented by another commander, by Commander Hadzihasanovic, and this videotape interview goes directly to that issue. It's not him being out of the country, it's who was in command of the army and the fact that they have put forth, on cross-examination, that he was represented by another commander. And it goes right to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand you. Are you saying in the agreed facts, the facts that were agreed to is the absence, not his lack of control?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, before I rule, you had something to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was just about to say that the colleague from the Prosecution said today that they agreed to the fact -- accept the fact that the general was out of the country. Also, in the pre-trial brief, and I cannot remember the exact paragraph at this point, this is also an accepted fact. This is just what I wanted to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if you just listen to the clarification that I got from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I was not really following because I was looking for this part of the statement. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It may take a minute to load.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "One must know that those operations had been planned for a long time, that I personally watched over every of those maps. They began on the 9th of September. That is the day after I had left for Malaysia. But they continued to be performed under my immediate supervision because the system of command and control functions, although one is not physically present at the site, because I was in continuous contact and secured that all that kept functioning. The presenter: On the other side you really achieved significant success. Delic: It has to be said -- "

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, you've seen that statement by General Delic, and I would like to know if you have any comment on what he has to say about being in continuous command while he was away.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any particular comment, because at the time I was in Kakanj, at the command post, at which time we answered to General Hadzihasanovic. Whether and to what extent General Hadzihasanovic reported to and informed Mr. -- to General Delic, I don't know, because we received reports at the Operations Centre. General Hadzihasanovic was informed of them, of course, and whether he talked about them with General Delic, that is something that I cannot say. I can only speak about what happened at the Kakanj command post, where General Hadzihasanovic was the deputy commander and our superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May this video be admitted in evidence, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. This is not a sufficiently-established base for accepting this video as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what that exactly means, "sufficiently established base."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, is this General Delic on this videotape that you just watched? Is that him speaking?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was General Delic. But as I said, I'm not going into the substance of the talk. That talk can be interpreted in a myriad of ways. I only describe what was happening in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, just listen to the question. The question was: "Is that General Delic," when you said, "Yes," that was the full answer required. Carry on, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think the basis for admitting this videotape is for the purpose that the Prosecution has offered, and the Court may give it whatever weight it wants to give it, and there may be other witnesses who will come in and talk about this tape. But I'm not sure of the objection, that there's no sufficiently-established base. This is clearly General Delic, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. The document is admitted into evidence, and may it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number 622.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any -- Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: No questions. [Interpretation] I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Alija, I have just one question for you relating to an issue that has been brought up during this trial a number of times and an issue which I thought you might be able to shed some light over, in your capacity as head of the Operative Planning in 1995. The issue is that we have heard that the El Mujahid Detachment was resubordinated from the 3rd Corps to the 35th Division a few times, I think, in 1995, and my question to you is: Was that something that you knew about, and if so, were you involved in the decision to have this unit resubordinated from the 3rd Corps down to the 35th Division in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved. It was not within my competence. During the war, I had only heard of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, and I never saw any one of them during the war, only after the war, when this topic became more widely discussed, did I hear more about this detachment. And, Your Honours, I practically know nothing about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And you don't know anything about the decision to resubordinate this unit within the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will have just one question. But in view of the fact that we had not been informed that this video would be on the list, I ask for your permission to let me just ask one question in connection with the video which was used by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alija, you just saw a video clip in which, of course, you recognise General Delic. Do you remember that he said, "Control and command are functioning also when I'm not in the state"; do you remember him saying that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that, and I commented on it, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, is it not, that he had designated a person to stand in for him?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did, and we saw that in a series of documents here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that someone should designate someone to stand in for him means that the former person took care that control and command will function during his absence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you worked in an administration which, in a way, dealt with planning, I should like to ask you the following question: It is correct, is it not, that the maps which are presented to the Supreme Command Staff are the maps of the first subordinated command of the corps and not of the lower units; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Okay, now it's going beyond -- this is well beyond the scope of redirect, and it wasn't covered in cross-examination either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the video makes reference to control and command and to the fact that the general was pouring over the maps, and I don't see the point of this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We were interrupted. What I asked you was whether it was correct that the Supreme Command Staff had at its disposal the maps of the first subordinated unit, which was the corps, and approved those maps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maps of the lower units would not be submitted at any time to the command -- to the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they would not. They would submit maps to their superior commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And to latch on to that, in -- just another question in connection with the question asked by His Honour Judge Harhoff. As regards to resubordination, it's correct, is it not, that within the units of the corps, when units are resubordinated, which are directly linked to the corps, a decision as to whom, how, and in which way such unit will be subordinated is taken by the corps commander; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
