utterances.text: So the Supreme Command Staff can only decide on units resubordinated to it and not to those resubordinated to the corps; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That ends my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Sir, this brings us to the end of your testimony. I take this opportunity, on behalf of the Trial Chamber, to thank you for taking the time off to come and testify. You are now excused. You may stand down. And you may travel well back home. I just hope that those people who you thought might be of nuisance by asking you questions about testifying will not ask you those questions. Travel well, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honours, I've previously informed both the Defence and the Trial Chamber's legal officers, the next witness who was scheduled to appear tomorrow and Friday, PW-1, will not be called by the Prosecution. And for the record, when I say "will not be called," we will not be calling that witness tomorrow and Friday, nor will we be calling him at any point in the future. And to the extent that the Trial Chamber requires us to seek leave in order to drop a witness, I would respectfully request that I be permitted to drop that witness from the Prosecution 65 ter witness list. That, of course, means that we have no witnesses available for the remainder of this week, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You confirm, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That being the case, then you may take the witness off the list. That's it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could, I did have one or two other minor housekeeping matters perhaps I could raise at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because I'm forgetful, may I raise mine first, before yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The one I that I want to raise is yesterday you had indicated that you had something to raise at the end of this witness's testimony. Is this the point or was it something else? It didn't look like it was this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It was related to this point, Your Honours, in that it was a request for additional protective measures for the witness for whom we are not going to call. So yesterday's issue has become moot by today's issue -- by today's developments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. You saved the Chamber another decision. Okay, you can now go to the other housekeeping issues you wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have two things with respect to the schedule for next week. The first concerns the pending motion concerning the videolink for DRW-3, the witness that we had filed a motion concerning a videolink for and who was scheduled to testify on Thursday, 25 October. We have been informed by the Registry that for a number of reasons, it is not possible to conduct a videolink on Thursday, 25 October, and we will consequently be attempting to reschedule that videolink testimony. And of course we'll supplement our previous filing with respect to a specific date that we would propose doing that, once we have confirmation from the Registry as to available dates. As a result of that, we will not be calling DRW-3 on Thursday, 25 October. We do have, however, another scheduled witness on that day, followed by a witness on Friday, the 26th of October. I believe we'll be able to complete both of those witnesses in that two-day period without any problems. So we certainly will have witnesses available both Thursday, 25 October, and Friday, 26 October, but we will not be calling DRW-3 on Thursday of next week due to technical issues which we've been alerted to by the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want us to dispense with this item first? I don't know whether Madam Vidovic has anything to say. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have much to say, but perhaps if the Prosecution could just please confirm that the two witnesses scheduled for Thursday and Friday are Sabiha Silajdzic Brkic and Goran Krcmar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could confirm that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. That was actually the next point I wanted to raise. The witness on Thursday, 25 October, is Goran Krcmar and the witness on the 26th is Dr. Sabiha Silajdzic Brkic. With respect, perhaps Your Honours have noted and the Defence have noted, Mr. Krcmar is listed on the schedule as a 92 ter witness, and to avoid any perhaps -- or to avoid any issues that might arise with respect to that, I would like to, at this point, simply inform the Chamber and the Defence as to the Prosecution's intentions with respect to this 92 ter witness, which is the first of what we expect will be several witnesses that we will use the 92 ter procedure, and so as to perhaps avoid any confusion or problems, when that witness appears and to get some further clarification, if need be, I'd like to explain how the Prosecution intends upon proceeding with respect to the 92 ter witnesses that we will be calling. That way, if there is a problem, we're dealing with it sooner rather than later. Based upon the practice of a number of other Trial Chambers, and in light of the specific language of Rule 92 ter, the Prosecution will proceed or expects to proceed as follows: Obviously, the witness, Mr. Krcmar, will appear in court. The witness will then be asked a number of -- a brief number of foundational questions with respect to the written statement, concerning the situation under which the statement was given, the fact that he's had an opportunity to read the statement, to make any corrections to the statement, questions to the effect that the statement was given voluntarily, honestly, et cetera. We will then tender the statement into evidence on the spot at that point in time after laying that foundation. It's our understanding, based upon the Trial Chamber guidelines, that we would be permitted to ask a few questions, highlighting a few portions of that written statement. And with respect to exhibits, we will then lay the foundation, question the witness about any exhibits that are listed for him or against him on the specific exhibit lists, and then assuming we have laid such a proper foundation, we will then tender those exhibits into evidence. That is basically, in a nutshell, how we understand and intend to proceed with the 92 ter witnesses. As I've indicated, he is the first one scheduled to appear, and I wanted to avoid any problems when he does appear to testify. We are in the process of identifying additional Rule 92 ter witnesses in order to expedite the presentation of the Prosecution case, and I will be meeting with my team during the course of the next two days in order to finalise the November schedule, which will include several other proposed 92 ter witnesses as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comment, Madam Vidovic, or Mr. Robson? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I could respond. From the Defence point of view, we don't believe it's a particularly good way to proceed, to find out on the day that the witness actually attends to give evidence, whether that witness will testify viva voce or pursuant to Rule 92 ter. The Defence needs to know in advance, we submit, so that we can properly prepare properly, whether it's a viva voce style examination-in-chief or whether we effectively have to take over the examination-in-chief and cross-examine during the same session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't have to take over the examination-in-chief, you just have to cross-examine, that's all. And I would like to be educated on how different preparation for a 92 ter witness is from preparation for a viva voce witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, what it boils down to is if the Prosecution calls a witness pursuant to Rule 92 ter, it seems they would lay some foundational questions, the statement would go in, and effectively perhaps with asking permission to ask a few additional questions, it would be straight over to the Defence. Then it's for the Defence to effectively pick out all the salient points contained within the statement. So what it means to the Defence is that it could mean that we have to examine -- cross-examine the witness for a substantially longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is there anything wrong with having to do it for a longer period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No, there's nothing wrong with that at all, Your Honour, there's no problem there, but we'd like to know in advance, before the witness actually turns up, so we would say it would be preferable for a decision to be taken before. Also, we would ask that the Defence have the opportunity to put forward submissions on the determination by the Trial Chamber as to whether the Prosecution be permitted to call the witness pursuant to Rule 92 ter or not. So certainly we would ask for an opportunity to put our point of view forward before you take that decision. As to how that is done, whether in writing or in oral submissions, we're certainly open to that question, but, Your Honour, I would submit that the proper way to deal with this is that the Prosecution make its application well in advance that a witness be called pursuant to Rule 92 ter so that the Defence can respond properly and the Trial Chamber can take a decision in advance of the witness actually arriving at court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want to talk or do you want me to talk? I'm ready to talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I defer to Your Honour, but I just wanted to ask -- mention something else, if I could have the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I neglected to mention, and I'm grateful to Madam Vidovic for reminding me, Mr. Mundis, in addressing the Trial Chamber, alluded to practices in other Trial Chambers, and what I failed to mention is that of course in this Trial Chamber we've already had a decision relating to Rule 92 ter witnesses, and on that prior occasion the Prosecution was required or certainly took the steps to file a motion, and the Defence responded in writing also. So I would submit to a certain extent a practice has developed in this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, let me say a few things first, before I suggest a course of action. First of all, in terms of Rule 65 ter, a 65 ter list is supposed to indicate which witnesses the Prosecution intends to call as 92 ter witnesses. Now, the crucial question at this stage would be: Is this witness listed as such on your list?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour, and I don't know the answer to that, I must admit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't know whether he's listed as such?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I don't, because the issue has just been raised since we arrived at court today, so I haven't had the opportunity to check that. But you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you are aware that this witness was going to come, and you should be sort of getting your ducks in a row in preparation for cross-examining him, so you should have seen whether he's a 92 ter or not a 92 ter witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly preparations are underway, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, let's get the question. Is this witness listed as a 92 ter, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the 26th of September, 2007, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking to redesignate a number of witnesses, both 92 bis and 92 ter. On the 28th of September, 2007, commencing at page 3222 of the transcript and running through page 3227 or 28 of the transcript, we had a discussion about that motion, and the Prosecution at that time withdrew that motion based upon what was discussed on the 28th of September, 2007. It was my understanding at that point in time that such a motion was not required, that it was up to the Prosecution to make such designations, assuming that the Defence had proper notice. I indicated at that time, and I think this is on page 3227, that the nine witnesses listed in that motion that we filed on the 26th of September, 2007, it was our intention to so redesignate those witnesses, so that the motion which we filed, although we withdrew it in terms of the substance, the witnesses listed, it was our intention to redesignate them either from viva voce to 92 bis or to 92 ter. That's point 1, in terms of notice. Secondly, with respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, wait, I must --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On our original 65 ter list, there were no 92 ter witnesses listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On the 26th of September, we filed our motion asking the Chamber for its authorisation to redesignate. Following the exchange that we had on the 28th of September, I indicated that we would withdraw that motion based upon my understanding from the Trial Chamber that I was not required to make such a designation. I then went forward and said the nine witnesses listed in our 26 September 2007 filing would be redesignated, as we indicated in that motion. So certainly as of the 26th of September, the Defence has been on notice as to which witnesses we would seek to call under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will also note that the calender, as previously circulated, clearly indicates Goran Krcmar as a 92 ter witness, at least the most recent version of that calender as circulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, my calender doesn't say -- oh, wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My calender is the 26th September calender, 92 ter. Okay. This whole discussion involves a whole lot of things. Nowhere in the Rules have I come across a provision that anybody -- any party who wants to call a witness, in terms of 92 ter or 92 bis, needs permission from the Court. The 65 ter list, which is decided upon by the party, states there, "This is what I'm going to call 92 ter, this is what I'm going to call 92 bis." Now, fine, I understand you didn't do that, and if you didn't do that, then I think Mr. Robson is right to ask to be given notice, sufficient notice, of intended 92 ter witnesses. I hear that you did say, on the 28th of September -- I may not remember, and I rely on you, and I'm not saying you are wrong. I understand that you may have mentioned then that the nine witnesses that were listed in the withdrawn motion were intended to be 92 ter witnesses. Maybe just for the sake of abundant -- to make it abundantly clear, if you can just make short notice to the Defence and give a whole list of the people you're going to call 92 bis and those you're going to call 92 ter and let them know that. Yes, I think that would resolve the problem. That is the problem they're asking for. They just want advance notice that a particular witness is going to be either 92 bis or 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely, and there's no dispute about that, in terms of us trying to provide as much advance notice as possible. And as I indicated, I would expect, by the end of this week, to have a schedule of all the remaining witnesses that we will be calling and a designation as to whether they are viva voce or 92 ter, taking us through the completion of the Prosecution case, so that there's no further confusion at all about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Subject of course to any further developments where time catches up with us and we have to redesignate additional witnesses as perhaps 92 ter witnesses. But it's certainly my intention that by close of business on Friday, to have a schedule that will take us through the completion of the Prosecution case with all of that information clearly listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would that resolve your problem, Mr. Robson? Your problem was advance notice?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. It would solve the problem, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: May I add something. Just for the record, I would like to express my view on this, which is that when a witness is called under Rule 92 ter, some limited direct examination may be conducted by the party calling that witness, but I want it to be made clear that such direct examination must be strictly limited to issues that have to do with clarifying a few, perhaps, uncertainties in the statements. It would defy the purpose of Rule 92 ter, in my view, if we were to accept a lengthy direct examination of a witness who's being called under Rule 92 ter. That's all I wanted to clarify. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think there's no dispute about that, at least from the Prosecution side, Your Honour. Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We concur with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Nothing further from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Nothing further. From the Defence, any housekeeping?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just perhaps just go back briefly to the point about the notice. As we understand it, once the Prosecution has filed its notice as to which witnesses it is seeking to call under Rule 92 ter and Rule 92 bis, the Defence should have the possibility of opposing that suggestion if it feels that such an approach is justified, if it has reasons for opposing the witness being called under one of those rules. So it's just something that we'd like to just state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Certainly there's a distinction, I believe, under the Rules between 92 bis and 92 ter. Certainly with respect to the 92 bis witnesses, they will be the subject of formal motions, with certified statements attached, et cetera. I don't believe there's any grounds or any basis for an opposing party to challenge the use of the Rule 92 ter when the witness is here and available for cross-examination. I just want to put that on the record right now. Perhaps that issue won't arise, but I simply want to state, in principle, the Prosecution is opposed to the notion that the cross-examining party could challenge the use of Rule 92 ter, because I don't believe there's a basis in law for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, maybe let the Trial Chamber not prejudge the issue. It looks like that might be a contested issue to be ruled upon. At this stage, the Trial Chamber will refrain from commenting. Okay. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's just one matter which springs to mind, and that is the use of witness statements made by another witness when cross-examining or testifying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't we have a written motion on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think a decision is coming, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So I just put on record that we're still -- I don't think that's duly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A decision is coming on that order. Thank you very much. The Chamber has not forgotten. Is that all?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the case stands adjourned to Monday, the 22nd of October, at 9.00 in the morning in the same courtroom. Court adjourned.
